blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running an end-to-end supply chain means holding, in your head, the whole journey from supplier to customer at once. It is not enough to understand each part in isolation. You have to see how procurement affects production, how production affects warehousing, and how a small slip in any one of them shows up, a few weeks later, as a problem somewhere else entirely.

Experienced supply chain leaders watch three things every week: flow, inventory and customer impact. Is everything moving at roughly the right pace? Is stock piling up or thinning out? And are customers starting to complain?

An end-to-end view is the difference between fixing symptoms and fixing causes. The ones who master it are worth their weight in gold.

items.q: According to the text, why is it not enough to understand each part in isolation?
options: Because a slip in one part shows up later as a problem elsewhere
Because procurement is the only part that matters
Because each part has a different manager
Because customers rarely notice internal problems
items.why: "a small slip in any one of them shows up, a few weeks later, as a problem somewhere else entirely."

items.q: Which three things do experienced leaders watch every week?
items.why: "leaders watch three things every week: flow, inventory and customer impact."

items.q: The text says an end-to-end view is the difference between…
items.why: "the difference between fixing symptoms and fixing causes."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Seeing the whole chain helps you find real causes.
Watching inventory weekly gives useful early signals.
A leader should optimise each department separately and independently.
Problems in one stage can appear later in another stage.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo defende ver o sistema inteiro, não otimizar partes isoladas.

items.q: "The ones who master it are worth their weight in gold" suggests that…
options: supply chain roles pay in commodities
such leaders are rare and highly valuable
most managers already have this skill
items.why: Inferência: a expressão indica raridade e alto valor de quem domina a visão de ponta a ponta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James orientando a nova diretora de supply chain. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, every Monday morning, before the emails, before the meetings, you sit down for thirty minutes and you read the whole chain in one glance. That's the habit I want you to build.

Right now, procurement is running late on two components. Nothing is on fire today — production is still moving, the warehouse looks full. But that delay doesn't disappear; it just waits. In three or four weeks it becomes a delivery you can't make, and by then everyone is arguing about who broke it.

Look at inventory the same way. If stock is piling up in one region, something downstream has slowed. If it's thinning out near a deadline, trouble is already on its way. The number itself isn't the point — it's the signal underneath it.

And here's the part most people miss. When a customer complains, the instinct is to fix the complaint. Don't stop there. Trace it back. Ask what, three weeks ago, quietly went wrong. Do that every week and you stop firefighting symptoms — you start removing causes. That's the whole job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What habit does James want the new director to build?
options: A monthly report to the board
A daily call with every supplier
A thirty-minute Monday review of the whole chain
Answering all emails before any meeting
items.why: "every Monday morning… you sit down for thirty minutes and you read the whole chain in one glance."

items.q: What is the current situation with procurement?
options: It is running late on two components
items.why: "procurement is running late on two components."

items.q: According to James, what does a procurement delay eventually become?
items.why: "In three or four weeks it becomes a delivery you can't make."

items.q: When James says "the number itself isn't the point — it's the signal underneath it", he means…
options: signals are less reliable than numbers
the value matters less than what the change is telling you
you should track fewer numbers overall
items.why: Inferência: o estoque importa como sinal do que está acontecendo a montante ou a jusante, não como valor isolado.

items.q: What is James's main message about handling customer complaints?
options: Resolve the complaint and move on quickly
Escalate every complaint to senior management
Trace it back to the cause instead of just fixing the symptom
items.why: Inferência: "Don't stop there. Trace it back… you stop firefighting symptoms — you start removing causes."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need an end-to-end view of the process." End-to-end means…
options: from start to finish, the whole journey
items.why: End-to-end = de ponta a ponta, a jornada inteira.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A single ___ in procurement can cause a delivery failure weeks later."
items.why: Slip = deslize; um pequeno erro que reaparece depois.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Stock is ___ near the deadline, so we may run out."
items.why: Thin out = rarear; o estoque está diminuindo perto do prazo.

items.q: "They keep fixing the symptom instead of the cause." This contrast is between…
options: the visible sign of a problem and its real source
items.why: Symptom = sintoma (o sinal visível); cause = causa (a origem real).

items.q: "The ones who master the whole chain are irreplaceable." To master means to…
options: gain full command of a skill
items.why: To master = dominar, ter pleno domínio de algo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de operações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Inventory is starting to pile up in the northern warehouse." To pile up means to…
items.why: Pile up = acumular-se, formar uma pilha crescente.

items.q: "The director wants to get ahead of the delay before it hits delivery." This means to…
options: deal with it before it becomes a bigger problem
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se a um problema antes que ele cresça.

items.q: "Stop firefighting and look for the root cause." Firefighting here means…
options: reacting to one urgent problem after another
items.why: Firefighting = apagar incêndios, reagir a urgências em vez de tratar a causa.

items.q: "We need to trace back the complaint to what went wrong." To trace back means to…
items.why: Trace back = rastrear até a origem, seguir o problema até a causa.

items.q: "A weekly review helps you stay on top of the whole chain." To stay on top of means to…
options: remain in full control and up to date
items.why: Stay on top of = manter-se no controle e a par de tudo.
